editorial:
Ever wonder how they actually filmed a bus moving at fifty miles per hour without killing everyone on set? You get to find out in this cool HBO special. Instead of a boring history lesson, you have the legendary Dennis Hopper leading the way. He takes you behind the scenes of the 1994 hit Speed, showing you the chaos and the magic that happened off-camera. It feels like you are hanging out with the crew, getting a first-hand look at how they pulled off those crazy stunts and high-tension scenes. 

The best part is seeing the raw out-takes and hearing the actors talk about their nerves. It is fast-paced and funny, though some of the interview segments feel a bit dated. If you love seeing how movie magic works, you have to check this out. You can find it on some digital rental platforms or hunt for the DVD to add to your physical collection. If you can find a high-def version on a streaming service, it makes those old set photos look much sharper. It is a great companion piece to the original movie.
endingExplained: The documentary wraps up by showing the final results of the bus jump and the subway crash. You see how the special effects team used real models and clever camera tricks to make the action look real. It ends with the cast reflecting on the movie's huge success. You learn that the tension on screen was often mirrored by the stress of the crew trying to get the shots right on a tight budget.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves action movies and movie trivia
